---

## 🔴 Errors (likely broken or will cause build failures / incorrect behaviour)

### 🔴 E1 — `Directory.Build.props`: TFM-conditional property silently dead (AP-21)

**File:** `Directory.Build.props`, lines 10–12

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** During `.props` evaluation, `$(TargetFramework)` is **empty** for single-targeting projects (it is resolved later by the SDK's inner build dispatch). Since both LibA and LibB are `net8.0`-only, this condition never matches and `GenerateDocumentationFile` is never set. This is the classic AP-21 anti-pattern.

**Fix:** Move the TFM-conditional `PropertyGroup` to `Directory.Build.targets`, which is imported after the SDK has resolved `$(TargetFramework)`:

```xml
<!-- Directory.Build.targets -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

**File:** `Directory.Build.targets`, lines 6–10

<PropertyGroup>

  <Company>Contoso</Company>
  ...
</PropertyGroup>
```

This means the `TreatWarningsAsErrors=true` set here silently **overwrites** LibB's explicit `TreatWarningsAsErrors=false` (LibB.csproj line 13). The developer intent to suppress warnings-as-errors in LibB is defeated. This is a last-write-wins evaluation-order bug.

**Fix:** Move all of these **default** properties to `Directory.Build.props` (which is imported *before* the project file), using conditional defaults so projects can still override them:

```xml

  <TreatWarningsAsErrors Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''">true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company Condition="'$(Company)' == ''">Contoso</Company>
  <Authors Condition="'$(Authors)' == ''">Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright Condition="'$(Copyright)' == ''">Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

**File:** `LibA.csproj`, line 14

<DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

**Problem:** This **replaces** the entire `DefineConstants` value, destroying the SDK-provided `TRACE` and `DEBUG` constants. Any `#if DEBUG` or `#if TRACE` checks in code will silently evaluate to `false`.

**Fix:** Append instead:

**File:** `LibA.csproj`, line 13

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">

**Fix:**

<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
```

<Compile Include="Class1.cs" />

<ItemGroup>

</ItemGroup>
```

---

### 🟡 W4 — `LibA.csproj`: Legacy `<Reference>` with `HintPath` to `packages\` folder

**File:** `LibA.csproj`, lines 27–30

```xml
<Reference Include="Newtonsoft.Json">
  <HintPath>..\packages\Newtonsoft.Json.13.0.3\lib\net6.0\Newtonsoft.Json.dll</HintPath>
</Reference>
```

**Problem:** This is an SDK-style project using a legacy `packages.config`-style assembly reference. The `packages\` folder layout is from the old NuGet model. This bypasses `PackageReference` restore entirely — the DLL will be missing on any machine that hasn't manually restored to that path. It also references the `net6.0` build of Newtonsoft.Json in a `net8.0` project.

**Fix:** Replace with a proper PackageReference:
```xml
<PackageReference Include="Newtonsoft.Json" Version="13.0.3" />
```

---

**File:** `LibA.csproj`, lines 32–34

```xml
<Target Name="PrintVersion" BeforeTargets="Build">
  <Exec Command="echo Building version 1.0.0" />
</Target>
```

**Problem:** Without `Inputs`/`Outputs`, this target runs on **every** build, breaking incremental build optimisation. It also has a hardcoded version string rather than using `$(Version)` or `$(AssemblyVersion)`.

**Fix (minor):** If this is diagnostic output, it's acceptable to always run. But the version should come from a property:
```xml

```

The solution has package versions specified inline (StyleCop in `Directory.Build.props`, Newtonsoft.Json via `HintPath` in LibA). As the solution grows, a `Directory.Packages.props` with `<ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>true</ManagePackageVersionsCentrally>` will prevent version drift.
